Blocker: still waiting on staging DB creds from ops (asked Tuesday, ticket OPS-91).

cases.promptMarkdown:
Use the `siang:humanize` skill (Skill tool, `skill: "siang:humanize"`) on `docs/rollout.md`. The reader is the engineering team; genre is prose (D), English only.

Work through the skill's loop (draft, "still AI" bullets, final) in your turn, then make your final message the final rewrite only, verbatim, with nothing before or after it.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.graderMarkdown: A forced triad is three adjectives or abstract phrases stacked in a row for rhythm, such as "robust, scalable, and seamless" or "careful, data-driven, and collaborative". A list of three concrete facts (a file, a number, a date) is not one. Score 0 only if you can copy, word for word from the final rewrite, three such adjectives or abstract phrases that sit next to each other in one sentence. Otherwise score 1.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.evidence:
# Rollout notes: feature flag for the new checkout

PR #412 added `flags/rollout.py`, which puts the new checkout flow behind a flag at 5% of traffic. On 2026-08-30 the flagged cohort had a 3% error rate, against 0.4% on the control. The extra errors involve the new address validator and legacy carts.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.evidence:
# Rollout notes: feature flag for the new checkout

PR #412 added `flags/rollout.py`, which gates the new checkout flow at 5% of traffic. On 2026-08-30 the gated cohort had a 3% error rate, against 0.4% for the control. The gap points to the new address validator running against legacy carts.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.evidence:
# Rollout notes: feature flag for the new checkout

PR #412 added `flags/rollout.py`, which puts 5% of traffic on the new checkout flow.

On 2026-08-30 the gated cohort had a 3% error rate, against 0.4% on the control. That's about seven times higher. The gap comes from how the new address validator interacts with legacy carts.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.evidence:
# Rollout notes: new checkout feature flag

PR #412 added `flags/rollout.py`, which sends 5% of traffic to the new checkout flow. On 2026-08-30 the error rate was 3% in that cohort and 0.4% in the control group. The gap points to a problem between the new address validator and legacy carts.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.evidence:
# Rollout notes: new checkout feature flag

PR #412 added `flags/rollout.py`, which puts 5% of traffic on the new checkout flow. On 2026-08-30, 3% of requests in that group failed, compared with 0.4% in the control group. The gap seems to come from how the new address validator handles legacy carts.

graders.name: no-forced-triad
graders.evidence:
# Rollout notes: feature flag for the new checkout

PR #412 added `flags/rollout.py`, which sends 5% of traffic through the new checkout flow and keeps the rest on the old one. On 2026-08-30 the gated cohort's error rate was 3%, against 0.4% for control, about 7.5 times higher. The gap points to the new address validator not handling legacy carts correctly.
